## Data

```{r}
set.seed(2206)
n <- 2500
parcel <- data.frame(parcel_id=seq_len(n), rain=rbinom(n,1,.30),
                     fragile=rbinom(n,1,.35),express=rbinom(n,1,.25))
parcel$late <- rbinom(n,1,plogis(-2.1 + 1.15*parcel$rain + .20*parcel$fragile - .5*parcel$express))
parcel$damaged <- rbinom(n,1,plogis(-3.9 + 1.4*parcel$fragile + .3*parcel$rain))
parcel$complaint <- rbinom(n,1,plogis(-3.1 + 1.8*parcel$late + 1.6*parcel$damaged))
parcel$insured <- rbinom(n,1,.42)
head(parcel,6)
```

## 2.1 Probability is a business risk, not a prediction guarantee

$$
\widehat P(L)=\frac{n_L}{n}
$$

- $L$ = late delivery event.
- $n_L$ = observed late parcels.
- $n$ = all parcels in the data.
- the hat indicates an estimate.

```{r}
p_late <- mean(parcel$late)
c(late_deliveries=sum(parcel$late),total=nrow(parcel),late_share=p_late)
barplot(c(on_time=1-p_late,late=p_late),col=c("steelblue","tomato"),
        ylab="Share",main="Chance a random SwiftShip parcel is late")
```

## 2.2 Sample space and events

$$
\Omega=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}
$$

- $\Omega$ = possible late/damage combinations.
- 1 = yes.
- 0 = no.
- $(1,1)$ = both late and damaged.

```{r}
joint_counts <- table(Late=parcel$late,Damaged=parcel$damaged)
joint_counts
barplot(joint_counts,beside=TRUE,col=c("steelblue","tomato"),
        main="Four possible late/damage outcomes",ylab="Number of parcels")
```

## 2.3 Basic probability rules

$$
0\leq P(A)\leq 1,\qquad P(\Omega)=1,\qquad
P(A^c)=1-P(A)
$$

- $A$ = any parcel event.
- $\Omega$ = all possible delivery outcomes.

```{r}
event_prob <- prop.table(table(parcel$late))
event_prob
barplot(event_prob,col=c("steelblue","tomato"),
        names.arg=c("On time","Late"),ylim=c(0,1),
        main="Mutually exclusive outcomes must total 1",ylab="Probability")
sum(event_prob)
```

# 2.4 Complement rule: avoiding double counting

$$
P(L^c)=1-P(L)
$$

### What each symbol means

- $L$ = late.
- $L^c$ = not late.
- 1 = probability of all possibilities.

```{r}
not_late <- 1 - mean(parcel$late)
c(not_late=not_late,late=1-not_late)
pie(c("Not late"=not_late,"Late"=1-not_late),
    col=c("steelblue","tomato"),main="Whole delivery population")
```

## 2.5 Addition and multiplication rules

$$
P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)
$$

$$
P(A\cap B)=P(A\mid B)P(B)=P(B\mid A)P(A)
$$

- $L$ = late.
- $D$ = damaged.
- $\cup$ = either or both.
- $\cap$ = both.
- subtraction removes double counting.

```{r}
pL <- mean(parcel$late==1); pD <- mean(parcel$damaged==1)
pBoth <- mean(parcel$late==1 & parcel$damaged==1)
pEither <- pL+pD-pBoth
c(late=pL,damaged=pD,both=pBoth,either=pEither)
barplot(c(pL,pD,pBoth,pEither),names.arg=c("Late","Damaged","Both","Either"),
        col=c("goldenrod","steelblue","grey55","tomato"),
        ylab="Probability",main="Overlap matters")
```

```{r}
n_boxes <- 12; sample_size <- 3
ways <- c(combinations=choose(n_boxes,sample_size),
          ordered=prod((n_boxes-sample_size+1):n_boxes))
ways
barplot(ways,col=c("steelblue","tomato"),
        main="Three chosen parcels: does order matter?",ylab="Number of possibilities")
```

```{r}
conditional_risk <- with(parcel,tapply(late,rain,mean))
conditional_risk
barplot(conditional_risk,names.arg=c("Dry","Rainy"),
        col=c("goldenrod","steelblue"),ylab="P(late | weather)",
        main="Weather-specific late risk")
```
